facts.F14: Design source: docs/feature/story-6358-s02-metrics-pilot/feature-delta.md (Ratchet design R1 to R7, slices 6, 7, 9), recorded, not re-decided. Paradigm object_oriented. Every rule reads the compiled production assembly (Lighthouse.dll) through the existing IlDependencies (Mono.Cecil), never ArchUnitNET's graph, because that graph drops edges written inside async bodies in Release. The module is found by namespace: Lighthouse.Backend.Modules.FlowMetrics.{Domain, Application, Application.Policies, Adapters.Background, Adapters.Persistence}; outside = any type whose namespace does not match ^Lighthouse\.Backend\.Modules\.FlowMetrics(\.|$); composition root = Lighthouse.Backend.Program. Baselines are inline lists of full type names (R3, R4: outside dependent; R5: 'Dependent -> Target' pairs) compared both ways.
facts.F15: Rule owners (test supports): the module rules are added as new static methods on the existing Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/Architecture/FlowMetricsModuleRules.cs, each taking its namespaces as parameters (same shape as KernelRules: one definition run on real and made-up types), returning the existing KernelRuleVerdict carrier where no baseline is involved. The two-way comparison is lifted, not copied, from the private RepositoryLeakRatchetArchUnitTest.AssertMatchesBaseline into a new shared support Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/Architecture/InlineBaseline.cs (internal static, same message: newcomers named with the fix hint, stale entries named with 'delete'); RepositoryLeakRatchetArchUnitTest calls it and keeps its own six comparison tests. S1 creates InlineBaseline.cs and owns it; S2 and S3 only call it.
facts.F16: One oracle file per slice (lesson from feature B, where a shared oracle made earlier approvals stale): S1 FlowMetricsInboundDomainAndAdaptersArchUnitTest.cs, S2 FlowMetricsInboundApplicationArchUnitTest.cs, S3 FlowMetricsApplicationOutboundArchUnitTest.cs, S4 FlowMetricsUnitTestPlacementTest.cs, all under Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/Architecture. A later slice adds files; it never edits an earlier slice's oracle. Each oracle holds its rule on the real module with its inline baseline, plus made-up-types fixtures (types declared in the oracle file under Lighthouse.Backend.Modules.FlowMetricsFixtures.* and outside fixture namespaces, read from the test assembly) for: a newcomer fails and is named, a stale baseline entry fails and is named, a compliant twin passes. facts.F19: Formal verification: no checker selected. The claims are finite and decidable over the compiled assembly (set equality of a measured dependent list against an inline list; namespace membership); there is no state machine, concurrency, temporal or liveness claim, and no representation change. Their checker is the native NUnit rule run on the real assembly plus exhaustive made-up-type examples (newcomer, stale, both, compliant, async-only, empty). Probe: quint and agda are not installed (which: not found), java present; neither is needed by any selected claim. Liveness: not applicable, the rules are synchronous single-pass reads with no progress obligation.
